A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDSGen research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated channel-selection analyses and retained qualitative examples.

before.justification: V1 reports original VGGSound generation experiments, Flickr-SoundNet evaluation, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds human evaluations, FAD measurements, vocoder and VAE comparisons, and further component analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds an AudioLDM-VAE pathway using single-channel spectrograms without RGB-channel selection, and supports HiFi-GAN waveform reconstruction alongside Griffin-Lim (Sections 3.1 and 3.5). These extend the pipeline while retaining the Transformer, Reducer, temporal masking, loss and guidance procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VGGSound video-to-audio generation and Flickr-SoundNet image-conditioned generation/localization. The new listening tests, component comparisons and VAE variants assess the retained coverage; they introduce no additional dataset, domain or distinct input scenario.

E2.justification: The principal external baseline roster is retained. V2 additionally evaluates a neural-vocoder configuration of Diff-Foley alongside Griffin-Lim (Table 5), and naive-average and attention-pooling alternatives to the proposed Reducer (Table 11). Newly cited methods such as MaskVAT are not added to the reported benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds FAD evaluation and a listening protocol using 50 videos per method, five participants and 1-to-5 ratings for audio quality and audiovisual relevance. It also introduces 300k-step component/VAE comparisons and audio-VAE preprocessing at 64×816 with 816 latent tokens. The original dataset splits and main training settings remain documented.

E4.justification: V2 adds train-versus-test overfitting curves for full and reduced video features (Figure 8), reducer-pooling alternatives, two-versus-four decoder-layer tests, and vocoder/VAE comparisons. These substantially expand evidence about design choices and their tradeoffs. The existing masking-ratio, guidance and RGB-channel analyses are retained, with the RGB analysis relocated.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without comparable uncertainty reporting. V2 Table 6 introduces MOS means with ± quantities, and Section 5.4 specifies five raters. However, it does not define the ± statistic or introduce repeated-seed uncertainty estimates for the generation benchmarks.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark values are retained, but substantial results are added. V2 reports MDSGen-B FAD of 4.3788 with Griffin-Lim and 2.1610 with a neural vocoder, plus MOS scores of 3.66 for quality and 3.76 for relevance. Its 300k-step VAE comparison reports FAD 2.36 versus 1.34 and alignment 98.58% versus 96.52% for image versus audio VAEs. These are new configuration-specific results, not improvements over matched v1 runs.

T1.justification: The denoising objective and masked encoder/decoder expressions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the added Reducer explanations and VAE discussion are architectural or empirical, without new mathematical derivations or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract's headline performance claims, introduction's contribution bullets and Section 6 conclusions are retained. Appendix B adds a contribution claim that MDSGen is the first masked-diffusion video-to-audio model supporting both image- and audio-based VAEs, modestly extending the claimed scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly discusses the tradeoff between audio fidelity, alignment and computational efficiency, including hypothesized evaluator bias toward image-VAE spectrogram formats. Appendices A.1–A.3 expand the Reducer's local/global-information explanation and distinguish input-dependent attention pooling from learned fixed weights. These substantially extend interpretation beyond v1's retained limitations and explanations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, explicit Reducer wiring, HiFi-GAN training provenance and duration, and audio-VAE tensor/token dimensions. The appendix still retains future-release wording for code. V2 also omits v1's explicit instruction to replicate an image into pseudo-video frames; this is a documentation loss, without evidence that the procedure changed.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning against masked-audio research, discussing MaskVAT, SoundStorm, VampNet, MaskGIT, AudioMAE, SpecAugment and Bai et al. It distinguishes noisy latent-space diffusion from non-diffusion generation and clean-spectrogram representation learning. Additional references support the vocoder, VAE and future-direction discussions.

P1.justification: Much of the original prose and overall narrative remains unchanged. Local revisions recast Section 3.5 around VAE choice, move the RGB-channel analysis into Appendix A.8, and incorporate new evaluation and explanatory subsections. Conference-header, corresponding-author and acknowledgment text is also added.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displays with vocoder, human-rating, pooling, decoder and VAE tables, plus a Reducer diagram and overfitting curves. Table 1 gains FAD columns, and Figure 2 uses generalized dimensions and optional channel selection. The original RGB table and histogram are relocated as Table 14 and Figure 10; qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 materially addresses v1's lack of systematic perceptual validation through FAD and a 50-video, five-rater listening study. Controlled component comparisons and the VAE tradeoff analysis also strengthen the evidence for design choices. Reporting weaknesses temper these gains: MOS ± quantities are undefined, and Table 1 combines audio-VAE FAD with retained image-VAE metrics and 500k labels despite Appendix B's 300k description. These limit joint performance claims, but the new direct audio-quality evidence and diagnostic analyses substantially improve overall quality.
